queries.hook: The fire of having just walked away from security for something you believe in, and the resolve to keep it burning when the first hard month arrives.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at the old life; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about to enter the battle, telling him that on this path no effort is ever wasted. Even a little sincere practice protects a person from great fear. The idea is to do the work fully and let go of owning the result.
verse.for_you: You have left the job and are going all in. The fire is real. Do the work fully, even when the next month brings no money. Let go of owning the result.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

prasang.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where everything feels heavy and final. He is telling him that the person who acts without clinging to the result finds a deep, steady peace. The person who is desperate for the prize is trapped by it. The idea is to be fully inside the work without letting the mess soak into you. It is not about refusing a fair wage, but about not being chained to the outcome.
verse.for_you: You left with no income and you are building something that is yours. The fire you feel now is real, but the next months will ask you to work without the promise of a quick reward. Try to stay in the work itself, and let the result find you later.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from his quiet study, knowing that praise and blame are just noise. He says that fortune and even death may come today or ages from now, but the steady person does not step off the right path. The verse proposes that when you stay on the path, setbacks are short. They do not last for those who keep going.
verse.for_you: Your brand is your path, and the silence from the world is just noise. The hard months will come, but they will not last if you keep going. Hold to the work itself and let the rest of the noise pass through.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira in the forest. She sees him waiting for fate to fix their suffering. She says that working hard and not seeing results yet is not a reason to stop. Every attempt can end in success or in failure. The only way to be certain of a bad outcome is to do nothing at all. She tells him to do what is right without expecting a reward, and then to keep working as if everything depends on his own action.
verse.for_you: You are living in the hard part now. The steady work you do today is the path itself. Keep going, even when the results are still coming.

verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.

verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: Vidura is speaking to Dhritarashtra, who cannot sleep the night before the peace talks. He is describing the wise person. This person decides calmly and then begins. They do not stop halfway through their work. They do not waste time. They keep themselves steady. That is the mark of a wise mind.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

script: You left the job last week and are building your brand from nothing. You feel more alive than ever and you want that fire to burn through the hard months ahead.
Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, just before the battle begins. Arjuna is confused and afraid of what is right. And Krishna replies:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते, स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्.
In plain words: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.

This is about doing the work fully and letting go of owning the result. It is easier said than done. When there is no money, it is hard not to count every hour and worry about tomorrow. But the truth is that a sincere effort is never wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
Keep your focus on the work itself. Make your brand today. Let the income be a result of that, not the reason for it.
What is the one small thing you will build today?

depth.life: You are seven hours deep into building a brand with no income. The fire from quitting last week still burns, but the first hard month is already on the horizon. You keep asking yourself if this drive is discipline or stubbornness. You are staring at a screen or a notebook, wondering if the work you are doing right now will matter when the money is not there yet.
depth.points: What you are doing is not wasted, even if nothing comes back immediately. The work itself is the protection. The fear you are feeling is the fear of the future, but the text says the effort you put in right now shields you from that fear. You do not own the outcome. You only own the doing.
depth.practice: Set a timer for twenty minutes and do one small task for the brand without checking for any result or sign of progress.
depth.question: What is the one small task you can do right now that is only for the work itself?
